title: Framework common-version checker omits approved ModSecurity v3 provenance literals
observed_behavior: Scheduled Framework workflow run 29728340118 at master efdbcbd98afeed0f39f8912ce1140aaa5742f507 exits 2 in check-common-versions with four ModSecurity repository/ref aliases empty. The same failure reproduces locally with python3 ci/tools/check-common-versions.py --check --json --timeout 20.
expected_behavior: The checker must resolve the reviewed ModSecurity v3 approved literal identity before resolving aliases, and missing tracked provenance variables must remain fail-closed.
impact: A mandatory Framework master supply-chain provenance control is red even though the approved identity exists. It blocks current-master readiness but fails closed and does not evidence an active provenance bypass.
preconditions: Framework source is at GitHub master efdbcbd98afeed0f39f8912ce1140aaa5742f507.
ci/lib/common.sh defines the three MODSECURITY_V3_APPROVED_* literal identity values.
The checker resolves four repository/ref aliases through those values.
reproduction: Read failed GitHub Actions run 29728340118, check check-common-versions, for master efdbcbd98afeed0f39f8912ce1140aaa5742f507.
In an isolated worktree at that SHA, run python3 ci/tools/check-common-versions.py --check --json --timeout 20 with task-owned external BUILD_ROOT and state paths.
Observe exit code 2 and empty MODSECURITY_REPO_URL, MODSECURITY_GIT_REF, MODSECURITY_V3_GIT_URL, and MODSECURITY_V3_GIT_REF.
Inspect parse_common_assignment: literal values accept CRS_APPROVED_* and CRS_RELEASE_TAG but not MODSECURITY_V3_APPROVED_*.

evidence.command: python3 ci/tools/check-common-versions.py --check --json --timeout 20; GitHub Actions failed-log readback for run 29728340118
evidence.summary: The checker fails closed because four aliases are empty even though common.sh contains the three approved literal provenance anchors.

On exact Framework master 784977615acfc55567e37b863309abc4a38ac877, the original check-mode reproducer exits 0 with no missing required variable. All three approved ModSecurity v3 literals and the four dependent aliases resolve to the reviewed identity.

root_cause: parse_common_assignment restricts literal assignments to CRS_APPROVED_* and CRS_RELEASE_TAG. MODSECURITY_V3_APPROVED_REPO_URL, MODSECURITY_V3_APPROVED_COMMIT, and MODSECURITY_V3_RELEASE_TAG are therefore absent from the resolver map, so the alias defaults resolve to empty.
proposed_remediation: Extend only the explicit approved-literal allowlist with the three MODSECURITY_V3_APPROVED_* identity names and add a focused literal-and-alias regression. Do not mark aliases optional, relax tracked-variable validation, change common.sh provenance pins, or alter MRTS.
acceptance_criteria: The parser resolves all three MODSECURITY_V3_APPROVED_* literal anchors and all four dependent aliases from a focused fixture.
validate_entries reports no missing variable for a fixture with approved literals and alias defaults.
A fixture without approved anchors still leaves required aliases empty and is rejected by existing fail-closed validation.
The candidate checker reproduction no longer exits 2 for missing ModSecurity provenance variables.
No optional-variable list, provenance pin, Sonar setting, Parent file, or MRTS file is changed.
validation_plan: Run the focused common-version provenance unit test with bytecode writing disabled.
Run Python syntax compilation for ci/tools/check-common-versions.py.
Run the Framework ModSecurity v3 provenance contract with external task-owned BUILD_ROOT and temporary paths.
Review the exact diff for parser allowlist scope and absence of optional-variable or MRTS changes.
After a Framework Draft PR is opened, collect exact-head CI, CodeQL, Sonar, review, and conversation evidence.
legitimate_control_tests: A missing approved anchor remains fail-closed through validate_entries.
The existing approved ModSecurity v3 repository, commit, and release tag remain the resolved source of the aliases.
No network lookup occurs merely to parse the fixture.
dependencies: Framework GitHub Actions execution for the exact Draft PR head
Current upstream availability for the common-version network checks
deduplication_note: Not a duplicate of FND-FRAMEWORK-0001, whose test-common/common-structure failures have a different cause, nor of FND-SONAR-0002, which owns the independent current-master Sonar gate. This finding owns the Framework parser omission that makes ModSecurity v3 provenance aliases empty.
evidence_limitations: The retained artifact is a sanitized local-reproduction and public-workflow summary, not a raw GitHub log export.
FND-FRAMEWORK-0028 separately tracks the partial automatic-update path that becomes reachable once the parser can resolve the approved literals.
Historical local and initial exact-head Framework Draft PR #36 evidence remains retained as a distinct lifecycle event.
Passing the parser correction and Framework PR-head SonarCloud check does not clear the separate Framework-master Sonar gate.

The master-only FND-SONAR-0002 result remains separately blocked, but the current user boundedly accepted it only for this protected #36 delivery; it neither waives PR controls nor blocks this finding's verified source-fix evidence.
No Parent gitlink update or MRTS action occurred.
residual_risk: A future common.sh layout or provenance naming change needs explicit parser review. The correction must stay restricted to the approved ModSecurity v3 identity names so arbitrary literals cannot silently enter the tracked resolver. Separate current-master Sonar issues remain blocked.

delivery_evidence.limitations: The exact resulting master was verified with the original non-writing check-mode reproducer. The separate FND-SONAR-0002 master-only Security E remains globally blocked and is not treated as a source-fix failure for this finding.
